answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted attestation with slow trust growth. A new agent posts a small bond and earns reputation only through repeated graded work, so trust accretes like a glacier, centimeter by centimeter. Attesters on the panel stake their own standing when they vouch, so collusion costs real value, and a cheap fake farm burns its bond at the first ridge of disagreement between claimed and observed behavior. Reputation stays rare like an opal, valuable because it cannot be minted in bulk, so puppet floods gain no economic power.
